title: Natural numbers and integers
competency: Tell natural numbers from integers and describe how the two sets are related.

keywords.def: A collection of well-defined, distinct objects. No object appears twice.
A counting number: 1, 2, 3, … The set is written ℕ.
A whole number or its negative: …, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, … The set is written ℤ.

en.text: Natural numbers are the counting numbers 1, 2, 3 and so on. We write this set as ℕ. Integers are the natural numbers, zero, and their negatives. We write this set as ℤ. Every natural number is an integer. But not every integer is a natural number.

am.text: የተፈጥሮ ቁጥሮች የመቁጠሪያ ቁጥሮች ናቸው፤ 1፣ 2፣ 3 እና የመሳሰሉት። ይህን ስብስብ ℕ ብለን እንጽፋለን። ኢንቲጀሮች የተፈጥሮ ቁጥሮች፣ ዜሮ እና አሉታዊዎቻቸው ናቸው። ይህን ስብስብ ℤ ብለን እንጽፋለን። ማንኛውም የተፈጥሮ ቁጥር ኢንቲጀር ነው፤ ግን ማንኛውም ኢንቲጀር የተፈጥሮ ቁጥር አይደለም።

screens.title: Counting sheep
screens.text: Kebede counts his sheep: 1, 2, 3, … He never counts 0 sheep or −25 sheep.
screens.ask: Which of 6, 0 and −25 could be a count of sheep?
screens.after: Only 6. Counting starts at 1. Read on to name these numbers.

screens.title: Sets of numbers
paras: Recall that a set is a collection of well-defined, distinct objects.
Distinct means no object appears twice.
In Grade 7 you met two sets of numbers.
ℕ = {1, 2, 3, …} is the set of natural numbers.
ℤ = {…, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, …} is the set of integers.

screens.title: Name the sets
defs: A collection of well-defined, distinct objects. No object appears twice.
A counting number: 1, 2, 3, … The set is ℕ.
A whole number or its negative: …, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, … The set is ℤ.

screens.title: Integer, not natural
screens.text: Which number is an integer but NOT a natural number?
screens.why: ℕ starts at 1, so 0 is an integer but not a natural number.

screens.title: How ℕ and ℤ are related
paras: Every natural number is an integer. We write ℕ ⊆ ℤ.
Not every integer is a natural number. 5 is natural, but −5 is not.
Picture a circle for ℕ drawn inside a bigger circle for ℤ.
screens.note: The book shows this diagram as Figure 1.2 in lesson 1.2.

screens.title: Sort the numbers
screens.text: Put each number in the right group.
items: ℕ starts at 1, so 0 is not natural.
Negative numbers are not in ℕ.
Negative numbers are not in ℕ.
screens.why: Natural numbers start at 1. Zero and the negatives are integers only.
screens.clue: Ask: could I count this many objects?

screens.title: Always, sometimes or never?
screens.clue: Look at where the list for ℕ starts.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: Every integer is a natural number.
screens.why: 5 is natural, but −5 and 0 are integers that are not natural.

screens.title: Lift buttons
screens.text: A lift in an Addis Ababa building has buttons −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4.
screens.ask: ___ of these buttons show natural numbers.
screens.why: The natural numbers are 1, 2, 3 and 4. So there are 4.
screens.clue: Cross out 0 and the negatives. Count what is left.
screens.worked: Cross out −2, −1 and 0. Left: 1, 2, 3, 4. That is 4 buttons.

items.text: Which of 6, 0 and −25 are natural numbers?
items.why: Natural numbers start at 1. All three are integers.
items.clue: Natural numbers are the counting numbers.

items.why: Every natural number is an integer: ℕ ⊆ ℤ.
5 is a natural number, but −5 is not.
items.clue: Try one positive and one negative integer.

items.ask: ___ of these numbers are natural numbers.
items.why: Natural: 8, 23, 534, 100. All eight numbers are integers.

items.ask: The last integer before one thousand is ___.

items.text: For any natural numbers n₁ and n₂, n₁ + n₂ is always a natural number.
items.why: For example 3 + 5 = 8. ℕ is closed under addition.
items.clue: Add two counting numbers. Can you get 0 or a negative?

items.text: For any natural numbers n₁ and n₂, n₁ − n₂ is always a natural number.
items.why: 3 − 5 = −2. So ℕ is not closed under subtraction.
items.clue: Try a small number minus a bigger one.

items.text: A triangle has perimeter 10. Its sides are natural numbers. Which side lengths are possible?
items.why: The longest side must be less than half the perimeter, so less than 5.
items.clue: In a triangle, the two short sides must add to more than the long side.

items.text: m and n are positive integers with m + n < 10.
items.clue: List the products for m = 1, then m = 2, and so on. Count each value once.
items.worked: m = 1 gives 1–8. m = 2 adds 10, 12, 14. m = 3 adds 9, 15, 18. m = 4 adds 16, 20. Total 16.

test.text: ℕ ⊆ ℤ means every natural number is an integer.
